title: A/B Experiment Control Plane: stratified bucketing, sequential checks, and auto-rollback
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a production-grade A/B control plane for model version experiments that supports stratified per-request bucketing, cohort-aware exposure throttles, sequential statistical checks (frequentist and Bayesian), and declarative auto-rollback policies. This ticket scopes the initial implementation: experiment configuration model, bucketing strategy, exposure controller, monitoring contracts, early-stop logic, and operator UX for starting/stopping experiments. Goal: enable safe progressive traffic shifts for model variants with measurable safety budgets and automated rollback when statistical or business thresholds breach.
background: Teams currently run ad-hoc model rollouts with brittle scripts and manual monitoring. We need a unified experiment API and control plane so product and platform engineers can: define hypotheses, schedule exposure ramps by cohort, enforce risk budgets, run sequential tests without inflating false positives, and have an automated fail-safe that reverts to the previous stable variant on regressions. This integrates with Redwood Dedicated and Private routing so experiments behave consistently across environments.
outcome_metrics: primary: top-line quality metric (per-customer task success rate)
safety: hallucination rate as flagged by eval hooks
cost: tokens per request and cost delta
acceptance_criteria: Declarative experiment manifest supporting: variant definitions, cohort selectors, initial allocation, ramp schedule, and rollback rules
Per-request bucketing library with deterministic, stratified assignments and sticky affinity for sessions/users
Exposure controller that enforces both absolute and relative exposure caps per cohort and globally
Sequential testing engine: supports group sequential alpha spending (O'Brien-Fleming/Pocock) and a Bayesian credible-interval early-stop policy
Auto-rollback workflow that can be triggered by statistical significance, safety signal thresholds, or operator override; rollback recorded with audit log entry
Dashboards and alerts: time-series of metrics by variant/cohort, cohort-level drift detection, and clear incident runbook links
End-to-end test harness that simulates traffic patterns and validates rollback triggers in staging
design_notes: Use consistent manifest YAML for experiment declaration; reuse rollout schema from rollout-service v1 but extend with cohorts and safety_budgets fields
Bucket key precedence: explicit user_id > device_id > session_cookie; fall back to request hashing for anonymous traffic
Store bucket assignments in KV cache for sticky affinity for 48h to avoid reassigning during a user's session
Exposure controller will expose a token-leaky bucket per-cohort to enforce rate limits without adding head-of-line latency
Statistical tests will run on top of an event-sourced metrics store to avoid double-counting and to allow replayed analyses
technical_decisions: Statistical engine: implement both frequentist sequential tests and a Bayesian alternative. Default to frequentist alpha spending for teams that require regulatory audit trails; offer Bayesian mode for faster early-stop when priors are available
Compute: run sequential checks in the analytics pipeline rather than in the inference path to keep runtime latency unaffected
Rollback: implement a multi-step rollback (soft rollback redirecting 100% of trial traffic to baseline model, then purge variant from router after monitoring window) to avoid flapping
Routing: integrate with Smart Routing so variants can be assigned to specific capacity tiers (e.g., dedicated nodes) during experiments
Safety signals: wire into Redwood Optimize quality monitors and the Console alerting layer for unified incident handling
tradeoffs: Consistency vs. speed: sticky bucketing increases stability of user experience but requires KV storage and may slightly increase request path complexity

Statistical purity vs. operator velocity: group sequential tests reduce false positives but slow time-to-decision; Bayesian early-stop speeds decisions but requires priors and is less familiar to some stakeholders

Automation vs. control: auto-rollback reduces manual toil and blast radius, but operators must trust thresholds. We'll default to conservative thresholds and require explicit opt-in for aggressive automation
implementation_plan: Phase 0 (spec): finalize manifest schema, define metrics contract and SLOs (2 weeks)
Phase 1 (infra): bucketing library + exposure controller + KV sticky store + routing hooks (4 weeks)
Phase 2 (stats): sequential testing engine + Bayesian module + integration tests with metrics store (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (ops): Console UI for experiment creation, dashboards, and rollback controls; alerting + runbooks (3 weeks)
Phase 4 (pilot): run two pilot experiments with internal teams and dedicated capacity; iterate on thresholds and UX (2 weeks)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positive rollbacks from noisy metrics -> Mitigation: require multiple signals (statistical + safety metric + human ack) for auto-rollback in first release
Risk: increased latency due to bucketing -> Mitigation: implement non-blocking async lookup to KV and fall back to deterministic hash on timeout
Risk: data leakage between cohorts -> Mitigation: quarantine experiment metadata and mask identifiers in exported analytics; run privacy review before GA
Risk: operator mistrust of automated rollbacks -> Mitigation: provide clear rollback transcripts, two-step soft rollback, and an override path with audit trail
monitoring_contract: Per-variant time-series for each outcome metric (1m resolution) with p95/median buckets
Cohort-level drift signal (JS/KL) and anomaly detector with alerting threshold
Rollback trigger audit: record the exact rule and metric that caused rollback and snapshot current model/version + traffic allocation
Incident LD: include link to experiment manifest, recent PRs, and canary logs
qa_and_test_plan: Unit tests for bucketing determinism and sticky reassignments
Load tests to validate exposure controller under high concurrency and with burst traffic patterns
Statistical power tests using synthetic data to validate type I/II error properties under realistic effect sizes
Integration tests: end-to-end from experiment manifest to Console creation to auto-rollback in staging
Chaos tests: simulate metrics ingestion lag and ensure controller tolerates delay without premature rollback
